To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetic properties of the Precambrian mafic complexes in the Medicine Bow mountains of southeast Wyoming are: the remanent magnetiza-tion is approximately as strong or stronger than the induced magnetization; the magnetization of the Lake Owens complex is strong, 5.8 X 10-3emu/cc; the Mullin Creek complex is weaker; the Lake Owens complex has a surface outcrop corresponding well with the magnetic units, while the Mullin Creek Complex has a poor correlation between

1) the magnetic part of Lake Owens Complex is only about 2 km thick; 2) the magnetic part is about 1.5 times as thick as the outcrop; 3) the magnetic part corresponds with the outcrop; and 4) the remanent magnetism of Lake Owens Complex and the Mullin Creek Complex are in opposite directions.

the aeromagnetic anomaly overlying the Lake Owens Complex is due primarily to remanent magnetism and that the remanent magnetizations are strong enough to account for the long-wavelength anomalies in the region.

the magnetic properties of the Precambrian mafic rocks in the Medicine Bow Moun-tains.
the use of magnetic data in the interpretation of the geometry of the Lake Owens layered matic complex and adjacent bodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the magnetic properties of the Lake Owens layered maffc complex and the Mullin Creek layered complex are not consistent with the hypothesis that they are the source of the long-wavelength magnetic anomaly in this area.
the aeromagnetic anomaly is a good indication of the geometry of the Lake Owens mafc complex and that it is a good indicator of the presence of a separate, small mafic body northeast of it.

the Lake Owens mafc complex is a small, thin, strongly magnetic mafic body with a small, separate, strongly magnetic body on its northeast side and a weakly magnetic unit between the Lake Owens and Mullin Creek complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Lake Owens Complex is strongly magnetized with a remanent magneti- zation that is approximately as strong or stronger than the induced magnetization and that the Mullin Creek Complex is less strongly magnetized with an induced magnetization or viscous remanence in the direction of Earth's magnetic field.
the Lake Owens Complex is a strongly magnetized body, and that the Mullin Creek Complex is a weaker, less magnetized body.
the Lake Owens Complex is a strongly magnetized body, probably a mafic intrusion with some associated sedimentary material, that was emplaced at a depth of less than 5 km.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aeromagnetic data can be used to constrain the geometry and magnetic properties of the Lake Owens and Mullin Creek layered complexes.
magnetic modeling of aeromagnetic anomalies can be used to infer the magnetic properties and geometry of the Precambrian mafic complex.
magnetic anomalies over the Medicine Bow Mountains are not caused by a large, deep-seated mafic intrusion but are caused by the shallow Lake Owens layered mafe complex and adjacent smaller bodies.
